agent_notes: Change is additive: one new optional GeneralConfig field with a default. Existing config.toml files have no such key, so they load unchanged with 60.0. No public signature changes. No DB or schema impact (TOML config only).

Blast radius: GeneralConfig is imported by about 9 runtime modules and about 19 test files, but only through attribute access, so none of them break. The first UI settings save after upgrade adds `shutdown_drain_timeout = 60.0` to every user's config.toml, via _settings_to_dict's model_dump at routes.py:227. That is a benign file-content change. The float serializes the same way request_timeout already does.

Validator (ge=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False) tightens what config can set. It rejects 0, negatives, inf and nan, and the new tests in tests/test_config.py:175-197 cover each case. I found no bypass: pydantic applies allow_inf_nan to TOML floats `inf` and `nan`. There is no upper bound in the model; the comment says the UI ceiling (3600) belongs to the form, which does not exist yet. A large finite TOML value such as 1e9 would still be accepted. Once the field is wired, that would let the drain run until Docker's 90s stop_grace_period SIGKILL, which is the same as the env var path today.

Main interim risk (impact-001): routes.py save_settings rebuilds `general` from form fields and leaves out the new key, so a UI save resets any hand-edited value to 60.0. Wire the form field, or carry forward current_settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout, in the same phase.

DEFAULT_CONFIG template (triggarr/config.py:26-35) lists every commented general key but not shutdown_drain_timeout. The project convention is 'TOML comments preserved in defaults', so add `# shutdown_drain_timeout = 60.0` when wiring.
Performance: none. A single float field read at load or shutdown.
Verdict: safe to merge as a step part-way through the plan. Do not release until the scheduler reads the field (impact-002) and the settings save preserves it (impact-001).

findings.why_it_matters: If this ships alone, a documented config knob does nothing, and the README/compose guidance (stop_grace_period 90s > drain) cannot be tuned through config.

findings.problem: Before this change, an unknown `shutdown_drain_timeout` key in [general] was silently ignored (pydantic BaseModel's default is extra='ignore'). Those values were never supported (the key did not exist), so this is the control working as intended, not a regression. pending: show an existing deployment whose config.toml already has this key with a value below 1, inf or nan.
findings.title: Validator tightening: configs with shutdown_drain_timeout below 1, inf or nan now stop startup
findings.why_it_matters: A startup abort is the worst outcome on the load path. It only happens for values outside the field's contract.
